definition: The division of the skeleton consisting of the skull, vertebral column, ribs, and sternum — the bones along the body's central axis.
mnemonic: axis = "axle, pivot." The central axis of the body.

definition: The division of the skeleton consisting of the limbs and the girdles (pectoral and pelvic) that attach them to the axial skeleton.
mnemonic: appendere = "to hang upon." The limbs hang off the axial skeleton.

definition: The most common type of cartilage, glassy and smooth, found on articular surfaces and the respiratory tract.
mnemonic: Greek hyalos = "glass." Named for its glassy, translucent look.

definition: A flexible type of cartilage containing elastic fibers, found in structures like the outer ear and epiglottis.
mnemonic: Greek elaunein = "to drive, stretch." Named for its springy fibers.

definition: A tough type of cartilage with dense collagen fibers, found in intervertebral discs and the menisci.
mnemonic: fibra = "fiber." Cartilage dense with visible collagen fibers.

definition: An immature cartilage cell that actively secretes the cartilage matrix.
mnemonic: Greek chondros = "cartilage" + blastos = "sprout, germ." A cartilage-building cell.

definition: A mature cartilage cell, housed within a lacuna, that maintains the surrounding cartilage matrix.
mnemonic: Greek chondros = "cartilage" + kytos = "cell." A mature cartilage cell.

definition: A small cavity within cartilage or bone matrix that houses a chondrocyte or osteocyte.
mnemonic: lacuna = "pit, hollow" — a little lake, from lacus.

definition: The dense connective tissue membrane covering the surface of cartilage.
mnemonic: Greek peri = "around" + chondros = "cartilage."

definition: Porous, lightweight bone tissue made of a lattice of trabeculae.
mnemonic: also called cancellous or trabecular bone — Named simply for its sponge-like porous look; cancellous is from cancelli = "lattice, crossbars," describing the trabecular mesh.

definition: Dense, solid bone tissue that forms the outer layer of bones and the shaft of long bones.
mnemonic: compactus = "packed together, dense."

definition: Bone-building cells that synthesize and secrete new bone matrix. (Fig 2)
mnemonic: Greek osteon = "bone" + blastos = "sprout, germ." A bone-building cell.

definition: Mature bone cells, housed within lacunae, that maintain the surrounding bone matrix. (Fig 1)
mnemonic: Greek osteon = "bone" + kytos = "cell." A mature bone cell.

definition: Large, multinucleated cells that break down and resorb bone matrix. (Fig 3-4)
mnemonic: Greek osteon = "bone" + klastos = "broken." A bone-breaking cell.

definition: The dense connective tissue membrane covering the outer surface of a bone (except at joint surfaces).
mnemonic: Greek peri = "around" + osteon = "bone."

definition: The thin membrane lining the internal surfaces of bone, including the medullary cavity.
mnemonic: Inner lining of bone. "endo" inner, "osteum" bone

definition: The structural unit of compact bone, consisting of concentric lamellae surrounding a central canal; also called a Haversian system.
mnemonic: Greek osteon = "bone." The basic structural unit of compact bone.

definition: The channel running through the center of an osteon that houses blood vessels and nerves.
mnemonic: centrum = "center" + canalis = "channel."

definition: A thin, concentric layer of bone matrix surrounding the central canal within an osteon.
mnemonic: Latin diminutive of lamina = "thin plate." A "little plate."

definition: Tiny channels radiating from lacunae in bone that allow osteocytes to communicate and exchange nutrients.
mnemonic: "iculi" is diminutive in latin (small or tiny). "tiny" + "canal"

definition: A channel that runs perpendicular to central canals, connecting blood vessels and nerves across osteons; also called Volkmann's canal.
mnemonic: small canal, looks like a perforation between two canals.

definition: The interconnecting spicules of bone that form the lattice-like structure of spongy bone.
mnemonic: "trabis" like timber or beam, and "ecule" as a diminutive, meaning small. So "little beam" offering structural support

definition: The blood-cell-forming (hematopoietic) tissue found within spongy bone.
mnemonic: AKA myeloid tissue — Greek myelos = "marrow" (root of "myeloid").

definition: Fat-storing marrow found mainly within the medullary cavity of long bones in adults.
mnemonic: Named simply for its yellow, fat-rich color (adipose tissue replacing blood-forming marrow).

definition: The zone of the epiphyseal plate where chondrocytes rapidly divide, pushing the epiphysis away from the diaphysis.
mnemonic: proles = "offspring" + ferre = "to bear." Where cells multiply.

definition: The zone of the epiphyseal plate where chondrocytes mature and enlarge.
mnemonic: "hyper" = above / excessive, "troph" = growth. Excessive growth zone.

definition: The zone of the epiphyseal plate where mineral deposits harden the cartilage matrix, cutting off nutrient diffusion and killing the chondrocytes.
mnemonic: calx/calcis = "lime." Where mineral (calcium) hardens the cartilage matrix.

definition: The zone of the epiphyseal plate closest to the diaphysis, where new bone tissue replaces calcified cartilage.
mnemonic: cartilage turns to bone - AKA "bone"-ification — os/ossis = "bone" + -ficare = "to make."

definition: Bones that are longer than they are wide, with a shaft and two ends; e.g. the femur and humerus.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English, no unique classical root.

definition: Bones that are roughly cube-shaped, with similar length and width; e.g. carpals and tarsals.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English, no unique classical root.

definition: Thin, flattened, often curved bones that provide protection or broad surfaces for muscle attachment; e.g. the sternum and skull bones.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English, no unique classical root.

definition: Bones with complex shapes that don't fit the long, short, flat, or sesamoid categories; e.g. vertebrae.
mnemonic: in- = "not" + regularis = "regular, ruled."

definition: Small bones that form within tendons, near joints, to reduce friction; e.g. the patella.
mnemonic: Greek sesamon = "sesame seed." Small bones resembling sesame seeds embedded in a tendon.

definition: Small, irregular bones that occasionally occur within the sutures of the skull.
mnemonic: sutura = "seam, stitch," from suere = "to sew." Small bones found within the skull's sutures.

definition: The shaft of a long bone, composed mainly of compact bone surrounding the medullary cavity.
mnemonic: "dia" = through, "physis" = growth. growing through

definition: The rounded end of a long bone, composed largely of spongy bone covered by a thin layer of compact bone. Can be proximal or distal.
mnemonic: "epi" = above, "physis" = growth. the growth at the top of the shaft.

definition: A thin layer of hyaline cartilage covering the epiphysis of a long bone where it forms a joint with another bone.
mnemonic: articulus = "little joint." Cartilage at a joint surface.

definition: The remnant of the epiphyseal plate in a mature, fully-grown long bone, marking where growth in length occurred.
mnemonic: Same root as epiphysis (epi = above + physis = growth) — the fused remnant of the growth plate.

definition: The layer of hyaline cartilage in a growing long bone where lengthwise bone growth occurs; also called the growth plate.
mnemonic: Same root as epiphysis — the cartilage growth plate itself, before it fuses into a line.

definition: The hollow, central cavity of the diaphysis that houses bone marrow.
mnemonic: medulla = "marrow, inner part."

definition: A narrow, slit-like opening in a bone, often allowing passage of blood vessels or nerves.
mnemonic: fissura = "a cleft," from findere = "to split."

definition: A soft, membrane-covered gap between the not-yet-fused cranial bones of an infant's skull.
mnemonic: French fontanelle = "little fountain." A pulse could be felt there, like a bubbling spring.

definition: A rounded opening through a bone, typically allowing passage of blood vessels or nerves.
mnemonic: foramen = "opening," from forare = "to bore, pierce."

definition: A shallow, basin-like depression in a bone.
mnemonic: fossa = "ditch," from fodere = "to dig."

definition: A canal-like passage running within a bone.
mnemonic: meatus = "a passage," from meare = "to go, pass."

definition: An air-filled cavity within a bone, such as the paranasal sinuses of the skull.
mnemonic: sinus = "a curve, fold, bay, hollow."

definition: A furrow or groove on the surface of a bone, often marking the path of a blood vessel, nerve, or tendon.
mnemonic: latin meaning "furrow" or "groove"

definition: A prominent, narrow ridge of bone that serves as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: crista = "crest, tuft" (as on a rooster).

definition: A raised bony projection located above or on a joint, serving as a site for muscle and ligament attachment.
mnemonic: Greek epi = "upon" + kondylos = "knuckle." A projection above a condyle.

definition: A narrow ridge of bone, less prominent than a crest, that serves as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: linea = "a line," from linum = "flax, thread."

definition: A sharp, slender bony projection that serves as a site for muscle attachment; also called a spine.
mnemonic: Same root as spine — spina = "thorn." A thorn-like projection.

definition: A large, blunt bony projection found only on the femur, serving as a major muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: Greek, from trechein = "to run." Marks a running-muscle attachment.

definition: A large, rounded bony projection that serves as a site for muscle attachment.
mnemonic: "tuber" from latin tuber = "lump, swelling, knob", same etymology as root vegetables and tuberculosis

definition: A large, rounded bony projection that forms an articulation (joint) with another bone.
mnemonic: Greek kondylos = "knuckle."

definition: A small, flat, smooth surface on a bone where it articulates with another bone.
mnemonic: French facette = "little face." A small, smooth surface.

definition: A rounded bony projection, typically found on the proximal end of a bone, that forms part of a joint.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English — a round end resembling a head.

definition: An arm-like or branch-like extension of a bone away from its main body.
mnemonic: ramus = "branch."

definition: The immovable joint that connects the frontal bone to the two parietal bones.
mnemonic: corona = "crown." Runs across the head where a crown would sit.

definition: The immovable joint that connects the two parietal bones along the midline of the skull.
mnemonic: sagitta = "arrow." Classically likened to an arrow's path down the midline of the skull.

definition: The immovable joint that connects the parietal bones to the occipital bone.
mnemonic: Named for the Greek letter lambda (Λ) — the suture is shaped like it.

definition: The immovable joint that connects the parietal bone to the temporal bone on each side of the skull.
mnemonic: Same root — squama = "scale." A beveled, scale-like overlapping edge.

definition: The single bone forming the forehead and the roof of the eye sockets.
mnemonic: frons/frontis = "forehead."

definition: One of the paired bones forming the superior and lateral walls of the cranium.
mnemonic: paries/parietis = "wall." Forms the walls of the skull.

definition: The single bone forming the posterior and inferior part of the cranium, surrounding the foramen magnum.
mnemonic: occiput, from ob- = "against, behind" + caput = "head."

definition: The single, bat-shaped bone that spans the width of the skull and forms part of the floor of the cranial cavity.
mnemonic: Greek sphen = "wedge" + -oid = "resembling." Wedged between the other cranial bones.

definition: The single, spongy bone located between the nasal cavity and the orbits, forming part of the nasal septum and orbital walls.
mnemonic: Greek ethmos = "sieve" + -oid = "resembling." Riddled with holes (see cribriform plate).

definition: One of the paired bones forming the lower sides of the cranium, housing the structures of the ear.
mnemonic: tempus/temporis = "time" — classically, the place hair first turns gray.

definition: One of the paired bones forming the upper jaw and part of the hard palate and orbital floor.
mnemonic: maxilla = "jawbone."

definition: One of the paired bones commonly known as the cheekbone.
mnemonic: Greek zygon = "yoke." Joins/yokes other facial bones together.

definition: One of the paired small bones forming the bridge of the nose.
mnemonic: nasus = "nose."

definition: One of the paired small bones forming part of the medial wall of the orbit, near the tear duct.
mnemonic: lacrima = "tear."

definition: One of the paired L-shaped bones forming the posterior part of the hard palate and part of the nasal cavity.
mnemonic: palatum = "palate, roof of the mouth."

definition: The single bone forming the lower jaw; the only movable bone of the skull.
mnemonic: mandere = "to chew."

definition: The single, thin bone forming the inferior and posterior part of the nasal septum.
mnemonic: vomer = "plowshare." Named for its blade-like shape.

definition: One of the paired thin, curled bones forming the lowest projecting ridge along the lateral wall of the nasal cavity.
mnemonic: "concha" because its curled like a shell

definition: A shallow depression on the frontal bone within the orbit that houses the gland for tear production.
mnemonic: fossa for the lacrimal gland (lacrimal = tear).

definition: The paired, rounded projections on the occipital bone that articulate with the first cervical vertebra (atlas).
mnemonic: condyle = "knuckle"

definition: The large opening in the occipital bone through which the spinal cord passes to connect with the brain.
mnemonic: forare = "to bore, to pierce", like perforate. Foramen magnum = big opening

definition: The larger, upward- and lateral-curving projection of the sphenoid bone, visible on the side of the skull.
mnemonic: Descriptive — named for resembling a wing (compare Latin ala, the formal anatomical term for "wing").

definition: The smaller, more superior projection of the sphenoid bone, forming part of the floor of the cranial cavity.
mnemonic: Descriptive — the smaller, wing-shaped part of the sphenoid.

definition: The saddle-shaped depression on the sphenoid bone that houses the pituitary gland.
mnemonic: sella = "saddle", turcica = "turkish". someone thought this thing looked like a turkish saddle i guess

definition: The opening between the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid bone, allowing passage of nerves and vessels into the orbit.
mnemonic: superior = "higher" + orbita = "eye socket" + fissura = "cleft."

definition: The opening in the sphenoid bone through which the optic nerve passes from the eye to the brain.
mnemonic: Greek opsis/ops = "eye, sight."

definition: The flat, superior portion of the temporal bone that articulates with the parietal bone.
mnemonic: squama = "scale," like a fish scale — thin and overlapping.

definition: The portion of the temporal bone that surrounds the external ear opening.
mnemonic: Greek tympanon = "drum." Surrounds the eardrum (tympanic membrane).

definition: The dense, pyramid-shaped portion of the temporal bone that houses the structures of the inner ear.
mnemonic: petrous = "rock", named for its extreme density which serves to protect the inner ear

definition: A slender, pointed bony projection extending downward from the temporal bone, serving as a muscle/ligament attachment site.
mnemonic: named based on its resemblance to a stylus (stylos in greek) + "-oid" which translates to "resembling". Resembling a stylus

definition: The depression on the temporal bone where the mandible articulates to form the temporomandibular joint.
mnemonic: Mandible root + fossa = "hollow" — the socket the mandible articulates with.

definition: The bony projection of the temporal bone that joins the zygomatic bone to form the zygomatic arch.
mnemonic: Same root as zygomatic bone — Greek zygon = "yoke."

definition: The rounded, bony projection behind the ear that serves as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: mast = "breast" + oid = "resembling" process. appears breast/nipple-like

definition: The opening in the temporal bone through which the internal carotid artery passes into the skull.
mnemonic: Greek karoun = "to stupefy." Ancients thought compressing these arteries caused unconsciousness.

definition: The opening between the temporal and occipital bones through which the internal jugular vein passes.
mnemonic: jugulum = "throat," from jugum = "yoke."

definition: The canal in the temporal bone through which the vestibulocochlear and facial nerves pass.
mnemonic: internus = "inner" + Greek akoustikos = "of hearing" + meatus = "passage."

definition: The canal in the temporal bone leading from the outer ear to the eardrum; the ear canal.
mnemonic: externus = "outer" + Greek akoustikos = "of hearing" + meatus = "passage."

definition: The perforated, horizontal plate of the ethmoid bone through which olfactory nerve fibers pass.
mnemonic: Latin cribrum ("sieve") + -form = sieve shaped. It has many perforations like a sieve.

definition: The vertical plate of the ethmoid bone that forms the superior part of the nasal septum.
mnemonic: per = "through" + pendere = "to hang." A plate hanging straight down (forms the nasal septum).

definition: The triangular bony projection rising from the ethmoid bone that anchors the dura mater of the brain.
mnemonic: (crista = crest/ridge, galli = genitive of gallus, "rooster/cock"). Looks like a rooster's comb

definition: The curled projection of the ethmoid bone forming the middle ridge along the lateral wall of the nasal cavity.
mnemonic: Concha = "shell" (curled shape, see inferior nasal concha).

definition: The sockets in the maxilla (or mandible) that hold the roots of the teeth.
mnemonic: Alveolus = "little cavity" — "Dental" is from dens/dentis = "tooth."

definition: The extension of the maxilla that forms the anterior portion of the hard palate.
mnemonic: Same root as palatine bone — palatum = "palate."

definition: The opening between the maxilla and the sphenoid bone forming part of the floor of the orbit.
mnemonic: inferior = "lower" + orbita = "wheel-track" (eye socket) + fissura = "cleft."

definition: The horizontal, horseshoe-shaped portion of the mandible that forms the chin.
mnemonic: Old English bodig. Just the main mass of a structure — no fancy Latin/Greek root here.

definition: The vertical, flattened portion of the mandible that extends upward from the body to form the jaw joint.
mnemonic: ramus = "branch."

definition: The posterior projection of the mandibular ramus, consisting of the condylar neck and the mandibular condyle, which articulates with the temporal bone to form the temporomandibular joint.
mnemonic: Mandibular condyle = The rounded projection at the top of the mandibular ramus that articulates with the temporal bone. — Greek kondylos = "knuckle" (same root as "condyle").

definition: The internal canal running through the mandible that carries the inferior alveolar nerve and vessels to the teeth.
mnemonic: Mandible root ("to chew") + canal.

definition: The opening on the anterior surface of the mandible through which nerves and vessels pass to the chin and lower lip.
mnemonic: mentum = "chin"

definition: The single, U-shaped bone suspended in the neck that does not articulate directly with any other bone, anchoring tongue and neck muscles.
mnemonic: Greek hyoeides = "shaped like the letter upsilon (Υ)."

definition: The region of the vertebral column consisting of vertebrae C1 through C7, located in the neck.
mnemonic: cervix/cervicis = "neck."

definition: The first cervical vertebra (C1), which supports the skull and lacks a body.
mnemonic: Greek myth: Atlas, the Titan who held up the sky. This vertebra holds up the skull.

definition: The second cervical vertebra (C2), which bears the dens (odontoid process) that the C1 vertebra pivots around.
mnemonic: axis = "axle." The vertebra the atlas (and head) rotates around, like a wheel on an axle.

definition: The region of the vertebral column consisting of vertebrae T1 through T12, each articulating with a pair of ribs.
mnemonic: Greek thorax = "chest, breastplate."

definition: The region of the vertebral column in the lower back.
mnemonic: L1-L5 — lumbus = "loin."

definition: The triangular bone formed by the fusion vertebrae located between the hip bones.
mnemonic: Fusion of S1-S5 — From os sacrum = "sacred bone" — the reason is debated, possibly tied to its use in ancient sacrificial rites.

definition: The small bone at the base of the vertebral column, formed by the fusion of 3 to 5 rudimentary vertebrae; the tailbone.
mnemonic: from greek "kókkyx" meaning "cuckoo". They thought it resembled a cuckoo bird's beak.

definition: The rounded, weight-bearing anterior portion of a vertebra; also called the centrum.
mnemonic: Old English bodig. Just the main mass of a structure — no fancy Latin/Greek root here.

definition: The posterior, ring-like portion of a vertebra that surrounds and protects the spinal cord.
mnemonic: Vertebra root (vertere = "to turn") + arch.

definition: The flattened portion of the vertebral arch that connects the transverse process to the spinous process.
mnemonic: Lamina = "thin plate/sheet". Think laminate.

definition: The short, thick bony process that connects the vertebral body to the vertebral arch.
mnemonic: pediculus = "little foot" (diminutive of pes/pedis = "foot").

definition: The opening within a vertebra, formed by the body and vertebral arch, through which the spinal cord passes.
mnemonic: Vertebra root + foramen ("opening").

definition: The paired lateral bony projections of a vertebra that serve as muscle and ligament attachment sites.
mnemonic: trans = "across" + vertere = "to turn" — projections lying crosswise.

definition: The single, posterior bony projection of a vertebra, often palpable along the midline of the back.
mnemonic: Same root as spine — spina = "thorn."

definition: The paired smooth surfaces on the upper part of a vertebra that articulate with the vertebra above.
mnemonic: superior = "higher" + articulus = "joint" + facet ("little face").

definition: The paired bony projections on the upper part of a vertebra that bear the superior articular facets.
mnemonic: Same roots as superior articular facets + processus = "projection."

definition: The paired smooth surfaces on the lower part of a vertebra that articulate with the vertebra below.
mnemonic: inferior = "lower" + articulus = "joint" + facet ("little face").

definition: The paired bony projections on the lower part of a vertebra that bear the inferior articular facets.
mnemonic: Same roots as inferior articular facets + processus = "a going forward, projection."

definition: The opening between adjacent vertebrae through which a spinal nerve exits the vertebral column.
mnemonic: inter = "between" + vertebra root + foramen ("opening").

definition: The fibrocartilage pads located between the bodies of adjacent vertebrae that absorb shock and allow movement.
mnemonic: inter = "between" + vertebra root ("to turn") + discus = "disc."

definition: A spinous process that is split into two parts at its tip, characteristic of most cervical vertebrae.
mnemonic: bi- = "two" + findere = "to split." Split into two points.

definition: The paired openings in the transverse processes of cervical vertebrae through which the vertebral artery and vein pass.
mnemonic: trans = "across" + vertere = "to turn" + foramen ("opening"), plural.

definition: The tooth-like, upward-projecting process of the axis (C2) that the atlas rotates around; also called the odontoid process.
mnemonic: dens = "tooth." Also called the odontoid process (Greek odous/odontos = tooth).

definition: The smooth surfaces on the transverse processes of thoracic vertebrae where the tubercles of the ribs articulate.
mnemonic: trans = "across" + vertere = "to turn" + costa = "rib" + facet.

definition: The broad, superior portion of the sternum that articulates with the clavicles and the first pair of ribs.
mnemonic: manubrium = "handle," from manus = "hand." The "handle" of the sternum.

definition: The long, central portion of the sternum that articulates with most of the costal cartilages.
mnemonic: Old English bodig. Just the main mass of a structure — no fancy Latin/Greek root here.

definition: The small, cartilaginous or bony projection at the inferior tip of the sternum.
mnemonic: Greek xiphos = "sword" + -oid = "resembling." Sword-shaped tip of the sternum.

definition: Rib pairs 1 through 7, which attach directly to the sternum via their own costal cartilage.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English — these ribs attach directly to the sternum.

definition: Rib pairs 8 through 12, which do not attach directly to the sternum.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English — these ribs don't attach directly to the sternum.

definition: Rib pairs 11 and 12, which have no attachment to the sternum at all.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English — no anterior attachment at all, so they "float" free.

definition: The strips of hyaline cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum.
mnemonic: costa = "rib."

definition: The S-shaped bone that connects the sternum to the scapula; the collarbone. (1)
mnemonic: clavicula = "little key," from its curved, key-like shape.

definition: The flat, triangular bone forming the posterior part of the pectoral girdle; the shoulder blade. (2)
mnemonic: scapula = "shoulder blade."

definition: The single long bone of the upper arm, extending from the shoulder to the elbow. (3)
mnemonic: humerus = "shoulder, upper arm."

definition: The lateral (thumb-side) long bone of the forearm.
mnemonic: radius = "spoke of a wheel, ray." Rotates around the ulna like a spoke.

definition: The medial (pinky-side) long bone of the forearm.
mnemonic: ulna = "elbow, forearm" — cognate with the English word "elbow."

definition: The eight small bones that make up the wrist.
mnemonic: Greek karpos = "wrist."

definition: The five long bones that make up the palm of the hand.
mnemonic: Greek meta = "beyond" + karpos = "wrist." Bones beyond the wrist.

definition: The bones of the fingers or toes.
mnemonic: Greek phalanx/phalanges = "a line of soldiers." Bones lined up in a row.

definition: The shallow depression on the scapula that articulates with the head of the humerus.
mnemonic: Greek word glene = eyeball / socket. Also called the glenoid fossa

definition: The prominent ridge running diagonally across the posterior surface of the scapula. (4)
mnemonic: spina = "thorn."

definition: The lateral bony projection of the scapular spine that articulates with the clavicle.
mnemonic: Greek akron = "tip" + omos = "shoulder." The tip of the shoulder.

definition: The hook-like anterior projection of the scapula that serves as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: Greek kórax = "raven" or "crow". Same root word for "corvid". Means "shaped like a raven's beak". Coronoid process on the mandible and ulna make the same comparison. Cora -C- oid because its part of the s -C- apula

definition: The depression on the scapula above the spine.
mnemonic: where the supraspinatus muscle originates — supra = "above" + spina = "spine."

definition: The depression on the scapula below the spine.
mnemonic: where the infraspinatus muscle originates. — infra = "below" + spina = "spine."

definition: The concave anterior surface of the scapula, facing the ribcage.
mnemonic: where the subscapularis muscle originates. "Sub" used instead of "infra" because it's deep to the scapula. Infra / supra are used in reference to another landmark. — sub = "under" + scapula.

definition: The large, lateral bony projection near the proximal end of the humerus, serving as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: tuber = "lump, swelling."

definition: The smaller, anterior bony projection near the proximal end of the humerus, serving as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: Tuber ("lump") root — the smaller of the two.

definition: The elongated central portion of the humerus between its proximal and distal ends.
mnemonic: Plain English/Germanic, descriptive — a straight rod, like an arrow shaft.

definition: The bony projection on the medial side of the distal humerus, serving as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: medius = "middle" + epicondyle ("upon the knuckle").

definition: The bony projection on the lateral side of the distal humerus, serving as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: lateris = "side" + epicondyle ("upon the knuckle").

definition: The rounded, lateral portion of the distal humerus that articulates with the radius.
mnemonic: capitulum = "little head" (diminutive of caput).

definition: The pulley-shaped, medial portion of the distal humerus that articulates with the ulna.
mnemonic: trochlea = "pulley," from Greek trochos = "wheel." Shaped like a pulley.

definition: The depression on the posterior surface of the distal humerus that receives the olecranon of the ulna when the elbow is extended.
mnemonic: Olecranon root ("head of the elbow") + fossa = "hollow" — receives the olecranon.

definition: The disc-shaped proximal end of the radius that articulates with the humerus and ulna.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English — a round end resembling a head.

definition: The elongated central portion of the radius between its proximal and distal ends.
mnemonic: Plain English/Germanic, descriptive — a straight rod, like an arrow shaft.

definition: The bony projection near the proximal end of the radius where the biceps brachii tendon attaches.
mnemonic: Radius root + tuberosity ("lump").

definition: The pointed bony projection at the distal end of the radius, on the thumb side of the wrist.
mnemonic: Greek stylos = "pen, stylus" + -oid = "resembling." Shaped like a stylus.

definition: The proximal, posterior projection of the ulna that forms the point of the elbow.
mnemonic: Greek olene = "elbow" + kranion = "skull, head." The "head" of the elbow.

definition: The curved depression on the proximal ulna that articulates with the trochlea of the humerus.
mnemonic: Same root as trochlea ("pulley") — articulates with the humerus's pulley-shaped trochlea.

definition: The elongated central portion of the ulna between its proximal and distal ends.
mnemonic: Plain English/Germanic, descriptive — a straight rod, like an arrow shaft.

definition: The pointed bony projection at the distal end of the ulna, on the pinky side of the wrist.
mnemonic: Greek stylos = "pen, stylus" + -oid = "resembling." Shaped like a stylus.

definition: A boat-shaped carpal bone located on the thumb side of the proximal row of the wrist; the most frequently fractured carpal.
mnemonic: Greek skaphe = "boat, skiff" + -oid = "resembling." Boat-shaped.

definition: A crescent-moon-shaped carpal bone located in the proximal row of the wrist, between the scaphoid and triquetrum.
mnemonic: luna = "moon." Crescent moon-shaped.

definition: A pyramid-shaped carpal bone located on the pinky side of the proximal row of the wrist.
mnemonic: triquetrus = "three-cornered."

definition: A small, pea-shaped carpal bone that sits anterior to the triquetrum.
mnemonic: pisum = "pea" + -form = "shaped." Pea-shaped.

definition: A carpal bone in the distal row, located on the thumb side, that articulates with the first metacarpal.
mnemonic: Greek trapeza = "table" — a four-sided figure.

definition: A small carpal bone in the distal row, located between the trapezium and capitate.
mnemonic: Same root as trapezium + -oid = "resembling."

definition: The largest carpal bone, located in the center of the distal row of the wrist.
mnemonic: caput/capitis = "head." Has a large, rounded, head-like process.

definition: A carpal bone in the distal row, located on the pinky side, with a hook-like bony projection.
mnemonic: hamus = "hook." Has a hook-shaped process.

definition: The hip bone, formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium, and pubis; also called the os coxae.
mnemonic: coxa = "hip."

definition: The largest and most superior of the three bones that fuse to form the coxal bone.
mnemonic: ilium/ile = "flank, groin."

definition: The posterior-inferior bone of the three that fuse to form the coxal bone; bears weight when sitting.
mnemonic: Greek ischion = "hip joint."

definition: The anterior-inferior bone of the three that fuse to form the coxal bone.
mnemonic: pubes = "grown up, adult" — the area where pubic hair appears at puberty.

definition: The single long bone of the thigh, extending from the hip to the knee; the longest and strongest bone in the body.
mnemonic: femur = "thigh."

definition: The sesamoid bone located within the quadriceps tendon, in front of the knee joint; the kneecap.
mnemonic: patella = "small dish, pan" (diminutive of patina).

definition: The larger, medial, weight-bearing long bone of the lower leg; the shin bone.
mnemonic: tibia = "shin bone" — also "flute," since early flutes were made from animal shin bones.

definition: The thinner, lateral long bone of the lower leg, which does not bear significant body weight.
mnemonic: fibula = "clasp, brooch, pin" — paired alongside the tibia like a pin on a strap.

definition: The seven bones that make up the ankle.
mnemonic: Greek tarsos = "flat surface, ankle."

definition: The five long bones that make up the middle of the foot.
mnemonic: Greek meta = "beyond" + tarsos = "ankle." Bones beyond the tarsals.

definition: The bones of the toes or fingers.
mnemonic: Greek phalanx/phalanges = "a line of soldiers." Bones lined up in a row.

definition: The curved, superior border of the ilium, palpable at the top of the hip. (1)
mnemonic: Ilium root ("flank") + crista = "ridge."

definition: The large notch on the posterior border of the ilium through which the sciatic nerve passes. (7)
mnemonic: Greek ischiadikos = "of the hip" — root of "sciatica."

definition: The bony projection at the anterior end of the iliac crest, serving as a muscle attachment site and palpable landmark. (2)
mnemonic: ante = "before" + superior = "higher" + ilium root + spina = "thorn."

definition: The smooth, concave, internal surface of the ilium. (8)
mnemonic: Ilium root + fossa = "hollow."

definition: The rough, thickened bony projection of the ischium that bears the body's weight when sitting. (3)
mnemonic: Ischium root + tuberosity ("lump").

definition: The cartilaginous joint that unites the left and right pubic bones at the midline.
mnemonic: Pubis root + Greek symphysis = "a growing together" (syn = together + physis = growth).

definition: The deep, cup-shaped socket on the lateral coxal bone where the head of the femur articulates.
mnemonic: acetabulum = "vinegar cup." The hip socket resembled a small vinegar cup.

definition: The large opening in the coxal bone, formed by the ischium and pubis, mostly covered by a membrane.
mnemonic: obturare = "to block up, stop." Largely closed off by the obturator membrane.

definition: The joint that connects the sacrum to the ilium of the coxal bone.
mnemonic: Sacrum root + ilium root — the joint between the sacrum and ilium.

definition: The rounded proximal end of the femur that articulates with the acetabulum of the coxal bone.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English — a round end resembling a head.

definition: The narrowed region of the femur connecting the head to the shaft; a common fracture site.
mnemonic: Plain English/Germanic, descriptive narrow region.

definition: The large, lateral bony projection near the proximal femur, serving as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: Greek trochanter, from trechein = "to run." Marks a running-muscle attachment.

definition: The smaller, medial-posterior bony projection near the proximal femur, serving as a muscle attachment site.
mnemonic: Trochanter root ("to run") — the smaller of the two.

definition: The elongated central portion of the femur between its proximal and distal ends.
mnemonic: Plain English/Germanic, descriptive — a straight rod, like an arrow shaft.

definition: The rounded, medial projection at the distal end of the femur that articulates with the tibia.
mnemonic: medius = "middle" + condyle ("knuckle") — toward the midline.

definition: The rounded, lateral projection at the distal end of the femur that articulates with the tibia.
mnemonic: lateris = "side" + condyle ("knuckle").

definition: The rounded, medial projection at the proximal end of the tibia that articulates with the femur.
mnemonic: medius = "middle" + condyle ("knuckle") — toward the midline.

definition: The rounded, lateral projection at the proximal end of the tibia that articulates with the femur.
mnemonic: lateris = "side" + condyle ("knuckle").

definition: The bony projection on the anterior surface of the proximal tibia where the patellar ligament attaches.
mnemonic: Tibia root + tuberosity ("lump").

definition: The elongated central portion of the tibia between its proximal and distal ends.
mnemonic: Plain English/Germanic, descriptive — a straight rod, like an arrow shaft.

definition: The bony projection at the distal end of the tibia that forms the bump on the inner side of the ankle.
mnemonic: medius = "middle" + malleolus ("little hammer").

definition: The proximal end of the fibula that articulates with the lateral condyle of the tibia.
mnemonic: Plain descriptive English — a round end resembling a head.

definition: The elongated central portion of the fibula between its proximal and distal ends.
mnemonic: Plain English/Germanic, descriptive — a straight rod, like an arrow shaft.

definition: The bony projection at the distal end of the fibula that forms the bump on the outer side of the ankle.
mnemonic: lateris = "side" + malleus = "hammer" + diminutive -olus, "little hammer."

definition: The tarsal bone that articulates with the tibia and fibula to form the ankle joint.
mnemonic: talus = "ankle bone." Ancient dice were carved from animal talus bones.

definition: The largest tarsal bone, forming the heel of the foot.
mnemonic: calx/calcaneum = "heel."

definition: A boat-shaped tarsal bone located on the medial side of the foot, anterior to the talus.
mnemonic: navicula = "little boat," from navis = "ship." Boat-shaped.

definition: The largest of the three cuneiform tarsal bones, located on the medial side of the foot.
mnemonic: medius = "middle" + cuneiform ("wedge-shaped").

definition: The smallest of the three cuneiform tarsal bones, located in the middle of the foot.
mnemonic: cuneus = "wedge." The middle of three wedge-shaped tarsal bones.

definition: One of the three cuneiform tarsal bones, located on the lateral-central side of the foot.
mnemonic: lateris = "side" + cuneiform ("wedge-shaped").

definition: A cube-shaped tarsal bone located on the lateral side of the foot, anterior to the calcaneus.
mnemonic: Greek kybos = "cube" + -oid = "resembling."

definition: The tendon that connects the quadriceps femoris muscle to the patella, continuing as the patellar ligament.
mnemonic: tendere = "to stretch" + quadri- = "four" + caput = "head" + femur root — a four-headed thigh muscle.

definition: The continuation of the quadriceps tendon that attaches the patella to the tibial tuberosity. (4)
mnemonic: Patella root ("little dish") + ligare = "to bind."

definition: The ligament on the medial side of the knee that stabilizes it against outward (valgus) stress. (2)
mnemonic: medius = "middle" + collateral ("alongside") + ligare = "to bind."

definition: The ligament on the lateral side of the knee that stabilizes it against inward (varus) stress. (6)
mnemonic: lateris = "side" + com- + lateris = "collateral" (alongside) + ligare = "to bind."

definition: The intracapsular knee ligament that prevents the tibia from sliding forward relative to the femur; commonly abbreviated ACL. (7)
mnemonic: ante = "before" + crux/crucis = "cross." The front ligament of a crossing (cruciate) pair.

definition: The intracapsular knee ligament that prevents the tibia from sliding backward relative to the femur; commonly abbreviated PCL. (1)
mnemonic: post = "after, behind" + crux/crucis = "cross" + ligament.

definition: The C-shaped fibrocartilage pad on the medial side of the knee that cushions and stabilizes the joint. (3)
mnemonic: medius = "middle" + meniscus ("little moon").

definition: The C-shaped fibrocartilage pad on the lateral side of the knee that cushions and stabilizes the joint. (5)
mnemonic: lateris = "side" + Greek meniskos = "little moon."

definition: Thin connective tissue wrapping each individual muscle fiber.
mnemonic: endo- = within + mys = muscle. Smallest wrapping.

definition: Connective tissue wrapping a fascicle (bundle of muscle fibers); carries blood vessels and nerves.
mnemonic: peri- = around. Wraps around the bundle.

definition: Dense connective tissue surrounding an entire muscle.
mnemonic: epi- = upon. Sits on the outside of the whole muscle. Order: endo → peri → epi.

definition: A bundle of muscle fibers wrapped in perimysium.
mnemonic: Latin fascis = bundle, like the Roman fasces (bundle of rods).

definition: Dense regular connective tissue formed where all three muscle wrappings merge to attach muscle to bone.
mnemonic: Latin tendere = to stretch. Dense regular CT: fibers all run one direction to take pull.

definition: A single long, multinucleate skeletal muscle cell.
mnemonic: In muscle, fiber = cell. Myofibril = organelle inside it.

definition: The plasma membrane of a muscle fiber; carries the muscle action potential.
mnemonic: sarco- = flesh + lemma = husk. The fiber's husk.

definition: The cytoplasm of a muscle fiber, containing myofibrils, mitochondria, glycogen, and myoglobin.
mnemonic: sarco- + plasm = formed substance. Muscle cytoplasm.

definition: Smooth ER network around each myofibril that stores, releases, and re-takes Ca²⁺.
mnemonic: reticulum = little net. The muscle's calcium net.

definition: Inward tunnels of the sarcolemma that carry the action potential deep into the fiber.
mnemonic: T = transverse: runs across the fiber, at right angles to the myofibrils.

definition: Enlarged ends of the SR that sit against each T tubule and release Ca²⁺.
mnemonic: cisterna = reservoir. Calcium reservoirs at the end of the SR.

definition: One T tubule flanked by two terminal cisterns.
mnemonic: tri- = three: cistern + tubule + cistern.

definition: Long rod-shaped contractile organelle running the length of a muscle fiber, made of myofilaments.
mnemonic: myo- + fibrilla = little fiber. Smaller than the fiber (cell).

definition: Protein strands (actin and myosin) that make up a myofibril.
mnemonic: Fiber (cell) → myofibril (organelle) → myofilament (protein).

definition: Organelle that produces ATP aerobically; abundant between myofibrils.
mnemonic: mitos = thread + chondrion = granule.

definition: Red, oxygen-binding protein stored in the sarcoplasm.
mnemonic: myo- + globin. Muscle's own hemoglobin; makes red fibers red.

definition: Protein inside the SR that binds and stores Ca²⁺.
mnemonic: calcium + sequester = to lock away.

definition: Class of molecule that forms the main bilayer of the sarcolemma.
mnemonic: Every cell membrane = phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

definition: Repeating contractile unit of a myofibril, running from one Z disc to the next.
mnemonic: sarco- + meros = part. The repeating segment.

definition: Dark band spanning the full length of the thick filaments.
mnemonic: dArk. A band stays the same length.

definition: Light band containing thin filaments only.
mnemonic: lIght, thIn.

definition: Central region of the A band containing thick filaments only.
mnemonic: German helle = bright. Shrinks or vanishes in contraction.

definition: Zigzag protein disc that anchors thin filaments and marks each end of a sarcomere.
mnemonic: German zwischen = between. Z = the ends.

definition: Protein line at the center of the sarcomere holding thick filaments together.
mnemonic: German mittel = middle. M = the center.

definition: Outer region of the A band where thick and thin filaments both occur and cross-bridges form.
mnemonic: The only place myosin can reach actin. Grows during contraction.

definition: Band that does NOT change length during contraction.
mnemonic: Thick filaments never shorten, so the band they define stays constant.

definition: Structure found in the middle of each I band.
mnemonic: Z sits in the middle of I; M sits in the middle of H.

definition: Model stating that thin filaments slide past thick filaments while neither filament shortens.
mnemonic: I band and H zone shrink, A band stays: the filaments slide, they don't shrink.

definition: Motor protein of the thick filament whose heads bind actin and hydrolyze ATP.
mnemonic: myo- + -in (protein). The oar that pulls.

definition: Main thin filament protein, containing the myosin-binding (active) sites.
mnemonic: Red beads in textbook art. The rope myosin pulls on.

definition: Strand that covers actin's active sites at rest and MOVES to uncover them.
mnemonic: trope = turn. The door over the binding sites.

definition: Regulatory protein that binds Ca²⁺ and pulls tropomyosin aside.
mnemonic: The lock; Ca²⁺ is the key. Yellow knobs in textbook art.

definition: Part of the myosin molecule that binds actin and ATP.
mnemonic: The golf-club head. An ATPase enzyme.

definition: Giant elastic protein anchoring thick filaments to the Z disc; gives passive elasticity.
mnemonic: Greek titan = giant. Largest known protein; the spring.

definition: Protein linking actin to the sarcolemma; missing in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
mnemonic: dys- = bad + troph = nourishment. Named for the disease it prevents.

definition: Troponin subunit that binds Ca²⁺.
mnemonic: C = Calcium.

definition: Troponin subunit that inhibits actin–myosin binding.
mnemonic: I = Inhibitory.

definition: Troponin subunit that tethers the complex to tropomyosin.
mnemonic: T = Tropomyosin-binding.

definition: Synapse where a motor neuron meets a skeletal muscle fiber.
mnemonic: neuro + muscular + junction = NMJ. One per fiber.

definition: Neurotransmitter released at every skeletal neuromuscular junction.
mnemonic: ACh. acetyl + choline, the two pieces AChE splits it into.

definition: Swollen end of the motor axon containing synaptic vesicles.
mnemonic: Also called the synaptic knob. terminus = end.

definition: Membrane sacs in the axon terminal packed with ACh.
mnemonic: vesicula = little bladder.

definition: Gap between the axon terminal and the muscle fiber that ACh diffuses across.
mnemonic: syn = together + haptein = clasp; cleft = split.

definition: Specialized region of the sarcolemma beneath the axon terminal, bearing ACh receptors.
mnemonic: The plate where the motor nerve ends.

definition: Folds of the motor end plate that increase surface area for receptors.
mnemonic: More folds = more receptors = bigger safety factor.

definition: Ligand-gated channels on the end plate that open when ACh binds.
mnemonic: Nicotinic type. Ligand-gated: opened by a chemical, not voltage.

definition: Enzyme in the synaptic cleft that breaks down ACh.
mnemonic: -ase = enzyme; esterase cuts ester bonds. AChE.

definition: Ion that enters the axon terminal through voltage-gated channels to trigger ACh release.
mnemonic: Calcium event #1 (neuron). Event #2 is SR release in the muscle.

definition: Main ion that flows INTO the muscle fiber through the ACh receptor.
mnemonic: Na⁺ in → end-plate potential. Not calcium!

definition: Local, graded depolarization of the motor end plate caused by Na⁺ entry.
mnemonic: EPP = local and graded. It triggers the all-or-none muscle AP.

definition: Process by which synaptic vesicles fuse with the membrane and release ACh.
mnemonic: exo- = out + cyto = cell.

definition: Number of somatic motor neurons that stimulate one skeletal muscle fiber.
mnemonic: 1 neuron → many fibers, but 1 fiber ← 1 neuron.

definition: Process in which a nerve action potential produces an action potential in the muscle fiber.
mnemonic: Excitation = nerve → muscle handoff. Contraction comes later.

definition: Events linking the muscle action potential to Ca²⁺ release and filament sliding.
mnemonic: Couples the electrical signal to the mechanical one.

definition: Voltage-sensitive protein in the T-tubule membrane that senses the action potential.
mnemonic: Dihydropyridine receptor, named for the drug class that binds it.

definition: Ca²⁺ release channel in the SR that the DHP receptor tugs open.
mnemonic: RyR, named for the plant toxin ryanodine. Mutant RyR1 = malignant hyperthermia.

definition: Ion released from the SR into the sarcoplasm to trigger contraction.
mnemonic: Calcium event #2: from the SR, binds troponin.

definition: Structure that Ca²⁺ binds when contraction is initiated.
mnemonic: Not tropomyosin, not actin: Ca²⁺ → troponin.

definition: Attachment of a myosin head to an exposed active site on actin.
mnemonic: The myosin head bridges across to the thin filament.

definition: Pivot of the myosin head that pulls the thin filament toward the M line.
mnemonic: Like an oar stroke. Uses energy stored during cocking, not new ATP.

definition: Molecule whose BINDING to the myosin head makes it release actin.
mnemonic: Binding ATP = detach. Splitting ATP = re-cock.

definition: Step where ATP hydrolysis puts the myosin head into its high-energy position.
mnemonic: Like cocking a mousetrap: energy stored for the next stroke.

definition: Post-mortem stiffness caused by myosin heads unable to detach without ATP.
mnemonic: Latin: stiffness of death. No ATP → no release.

definition: Structure that thin filaments are pulled toward during contraction.
mnemonic: Everything slides toward the middle.

definition: ATP-driven pump that returns Ca²⁺ to the SR during relaxation.
mnemonic: Sarco/Endoplasmic Reticulum Ca²⁺-ATPase. Relaxation costs ATP.

definition: One motor neuron plus all the muscle fibers it innervates.
mnemonic: When the neuron fires, every fiber in the unit contracts.

definition: Increasing force by activating additional motor units.
mnemonic: Recruit more soldiers = more wires firing.

definition: Rule that motor units are recruited from smallest to largest as demand rises.
mnemonic: Henneman's size principle: pencil units first, dumbbell units last.

definition: Motor unit type with few fibers per neuron, giving fine control.
mnemonic: Eye muscles: a handful of fibers per neuron.

definition: Increasing force by firing faster so twitches add together before relaxation.
mnemonic: Sum = add. Signals sent more often, never bigger.

definition: A single contraction–relaxation cycle produced by one action potential.
mnemonic: Three phases: latent → contraction → relaxation.

definition: Delay between the stimulus and the start of tension, while E-C coupling occurs.
mnemonic: latens = hidden. Something is happening, you just can't see it yet.

definition: Staircase increase in twitch strength with repeated stimuli after rest.
mnemonic: German Treppe = staircase.

definition: Twitches stack with only partial relaxation between them.
mnemonic: Wavy line on the myogram: still some relaxation.

definition: Smooth, sustained maximal contraction with no relaxation between stimuli.
mnemonic: Also "fused" tetanus. tetanos = taut. Normal physiology, not the disease.

definition: Sarcomere length that allows the most cross-bridges and maximum force.
mnemonic: Too stretched = little overlap; too short = filaments collide. Mid-range wins.

definition: Contraction in which tension builds but muscle length does not change.
mnemonic: iso = same + metron = measure (length). Holding a grip.

definition: Isotonic contraction in which the muscle shortens while moving a load.
mnemonic: con- = toward the center. Lifting the dumbbell.

definition: Isotonic contraction in which the muscle lengthens while controlling a load.
mnemonic: ec- = out from center. Lowering the dumbbell slowly.

definition: Low-level tension at rest from motor units firing in rotation.
mnemonic: tonos = tension. Keeps posture.

definition: High-energy molecule that regenerates ATP for the first 10–15 seconds of intense activity.
mnemonic: Greek kreas = flesh. The immediate (phosphagen) system.

definition: Enzyme that transfers phosphate from creatine phosphate to ADP.
mnemonic: kinase = moves phosphates. High blood CK = muscle damage.

definition: End product of anaerobic glycolysis in muscle.
mnemonic: lac = milk (first found in sour milk). Not the main cause of soreness.

definition: Elevated oxygen use after exercise to restore creatine phosphate, myoglobin O₂, and clear lactate.
mnemonic: Excess Post-exercise Oxygen Consumption; the old "oxygen debt."

definition: Red, fatigue-resistant fiber type rich in myoglobin and mitochondria (Type I).
mnemonic: Dark turkey meat: legs standing all day.

definition: Pale, powerful, quickly fatiguing fiber type relying on anaerobic glycolysis (Type IIx).
mnemonic: White breast meat: short bursts of flight.

definition: Voluntary, striated muscle with long multinucleate cells.
mnemonic: Nuclei pushed to the edge; stripes visible.

definition: Involuntary, striated, branched muscle joined by intercalated discs.
mnemonic: Greek kardia = heart. Branched cells, 1–2 central nuclei.

definition: Involuntary, non-striated muscle with spindle-shaped cells.
mnemonic: Smooth = no stripes. Walls of hollow organs and vessels.

definition: Dark junctions between cardiac cells containing gap junctions and desmosomes.
mnemonic: intercalare = to insert between.

definition: Property shared by all muscle: responding to a stimulus with an action potential.
mnemonic: Respond, shorten, stretch, recoil = excitability, contractility, extensibility, elasticity.

definition: Property shared by all muscle: the ability to shorten.
mnemonic: con- + trahere = to draw together.

definition: Ca²⁺-binding protein that replaces troponin's role in smooth muscle.
mnemonic: Calcium-modulated protein. Activates myosin light-chain kinase.

definition: Swellings along autonomic nerve fibers that release neurotransmitter onto smooth muscle.
mnemonic: varix = swollen vein. Beads on a string, no motor end plate.

definition: Recording of the summed electrical activity of active muscle fibers.
mnemonic: electro + myo + graphy = writing. EMG.

definition: Metabolite whose buildup weakens cross-bridges during peripheral fatigue.
mnemonic: Pᵢ, left over from ATP splitting. A bigger fatigue culprit than lactate.

definition: Fatigue caused by reduced motor drive from the brain rather than the muscle itself.
mnemonic: Why verbal encouragement raised grip AND EMG in lab.

definition: Independent variable in Part 1 of the sustained grip-strength experiment.
mnemonic: What the experiment is organized by; grip and EMG are measured in each.

definition: Autoimmune disease in which antibodies destroy ACh receptors, causing weakness that worsens with use.
mnemonic: my + asthenia = weakness + gravis = serious. Drooping eyelids.

definition: Autoimmune disease with antibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels.
mnemonic: Presynaptic (Ca²⁺ in), vs. myasthenia = postsynaptic (receptor). Improves briefly with use.

definition: Bacterial toxin that blocks ACh exocytosis, causing flaccid paralysis.
mnemonic: Latin botulus = sausage (early outbreaks). Botox.

definition: Irreversible AChE inhibitors in pesticides and nerve agents, causing spastic paralysis.
mnemonic: ACh can't be cleared → nonstop stimulation. Treat: atropine + pralidoxime.

definition: Depolarizing neuromuscular blocker that causes fasciculations before paralysis.
mnemonic: Two ACh molecules joined. Holds the end plate depolarized. MH trigger.

definition: Non-depolarizing blocker that competitively blocks ACh receptors for intubation and surgery.
mnemonic: -curonium ending = curare-like blocker (vecuronium too).

definition: AChE inhibitor used to reverse non-depolarizing neuromuscular block.
mnemonic: Raises ACh to outcompete the blocker. Given with glycopyrrolate.

definition: Reversal agent that encapsulates rocuronium or vecuronium molecules.
mnemonic: sugar + gamma-cyclodextrin: a sugar ring that traps the drug.

definition: Inherited RyR1 crisis triggered by volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine: rigidity, rising end-tidal CO₂, hyperthermia.
mnemonic: SR leaks Ca²⁺ uncontrollably → nonstop contraction → heat.

definition: Drug that blocks RyR1 to treat malignant hyperthermia.
mnemonic: Stops the Ca²⁺ leak at the source (the SR).

definition: Nerve-stimulator test of neuromuscular block depth using 4 pulses.
mnemonic: TOF. Fewer twitches = deeper block.

definition: Muscle fiber breakdown releasing myoglobin and K⁺, risking kidney injury; can follow prolonged immobility on the OR table.
mnemonic: rhabdo = rod (striated) + myo + lysis = breakdown.

definition: Regulatory protein measured in the blood to diagnose heart muscle damage.
mnemonic: Cardiac TnI and TnT leak out when heart cells die.
